text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The environmental factor may be incorporated into the country's economic indicators by the turn of the century to reflect a true picture of progress, Economic Adviser to the government, Daim Zainuddin said.

-- Efforts by New Zealand police to have a Malasyia engineers extradited over last month's parcel bombing in Wellington, which injured two Malaysian students, may run into a snag because Malaysia and New Zealand do not have an extradition treaty, sources said.

-- The Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) forum should open its doors and admit new members when the three-year moratorium on membership expires next month, Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said.

-- The Securities Commission is working on a holistic approach to develop the Islamic capital market, its manager for product development, Nik Ramlah Nik Mahmood said. The agenda include the development and strengthening of skills and professionalism among market intermediaries, introduction of a sufficient number of instruments and ensuring adequate investor protection.
